appendOnly.note: This file is new. The first attempt's qualification, its sealed failure and the two determinism records were re-hashed immediately before the run and are byte-unchanged.

bootableClaimScope: The sealed arm64 image boots to its default target under Virtualization.framework on one development Mac, in a machine with no network device, no shared directory and no writable disk. It is not a claim about a clean Mac, about any other machine, or about the guest serving anything.

cleanup.note: The run wrote only into a scratch directory outside the repository: the console, the run receipt and the driver's result. Nothing of the machine was left running.

judgedTranscript.whyItDiffers: The judge reads the console as text, which collapses the 230 CRLF pairs the guest emitted into single newlines; 20409 minus 20179 is exactly those 230 bytes. The file is valid UTF-8 and nothing was dropped or replaced. Both digests are recorded so neither number has to be taken on trust.

judgedAgainst.note: The six conditions were frozen and merged before the run and are byte-identical to the first attempt's. The driver re-checked that immediately before starting the machine and would have refused on any difference.

knownAbsentAndStillAbsent.consequence: systemd cannot resolve boole-node or boole-native-checker, so the launcher's service-identity prerequisite will refuse. systemd-sysusers would normally create them at boot, and it cannot on a read-only root. This is recorded now so that refusal is a known result rather than a surprise, and so nobody later reads it as the image being broken.

passConditions.evidence: the host re-hashed both files and read the sealed digests
passConditions.judgedBy: the host re-hashes the kernel and the root disk immediately before configuring the machine and refuses to start on any mismatch; both digests are written into the run receipt

passConditions.condition: the machine is configured with no network device, no shared directory and no writable disk
passConditions.evidence: no network device, no shared directory, one read-only disk
passConditions.judgedBy: the configuration the host built is serialised into the run receipt and read back: the counts must be zero and the single disk attachment must be read-only

passConditions.judgedBy: the captured console shows the kernel banner and an EXT4-fs line naming the root device mounted read-only

passConditions.condition: PID 1 is the systemd that was built into this image
passConditions.judgedBy: the captured console shows systemd's own startup banner reporting version 255, which is the version the image carries

passConditions.evidence: the image hashed to 566614b67ea749ee0061d73aad4e3320f92fe7d352df29d11e4494a8c063d41b before and after

preflight.note: Twenty read-only checks ran immediately before the machine was created: the tree matched its remote and was clean, the record was at the digest it was merged with, the attempt was unspent, no result file existed, the three sealed images matched by size and digest, the six conditions were byte-identical to the first attempt's, and the declared machine was closed.

furthestBootStage.evidence: [  OK  ] Reached target graphical.target - Graphical Interface.
furthestBootStage.note: systemd queued a start job for graphical.target at 0.116s and the console shows it reached, so the guest ran its default target to completion rather than stopping at an earlier one.

launcherUnit.whatStartedMeansHere: systemd executed the unit's ExecStart. The unit is Type=exec and User=root, so systemd needed no account lookup to start it and the missing /etc/passwd did not block it. Started is not a serving state and is not read as one.
launcherUnit.whatWouldMakeItObservable: routing the launcher's output to the console the host already captures, or the authenticated host-guest transport MAC.4 is for
launcherUnit.whyNotObservable: The unit sets StandardOutput=journal and StandardError=journal, so the launcher's own output went to the guest journal. A closed machine with no network device, no shared directory and no writable disk has no channel out, and the run was stopped from the host rather than shut down from inside, so the journal was never read. The console shows no failed state for the unit over the 195 seconds the machine ran, and that is the whole of what this run establishes about it.

stopReasonAndExitStatus.detail: the run reached its timeout and the host stopped it
stopReasonAndExitStatus.note: The machine was stopped by the host at its 180-second limit, which is how this qualification is built to end: the guest has no channel to be told to shut down. A timeout stop is the expected ending and is not a failure of any condition.

unitsThatEnteredAFailedState.evidence: [FAILED] Failed to start ldconfig.service - Rebuild Dynamic Linker Cache.
unitsThatEnteredAFailedState.why: Rebuilding the dynamic linker cache writes to /etc, and the root filesystem is attached read-only. This is a consequence of the containment the run is there to demonstrate, not a defect in the image.

initrd.whyUnused: the guest kernel has virtio-blk and ext4 built in rather than as modules, so it can reach the sealed root filesystem without one. The initrd carries the same tree as a cpio archive and has no /init, so using it would mean adding a boot path this image was not built for.

whatThisFixedComparedWithTheFirstAttempt.cause: The root filesystem has no mount-point directories for the kernel's virtual filesystems. Its top level holds usr, etc, opt, var, boot and the usr-merge symlinks and nothing else, so there is no /proc, /sys or /dev for PID 1 to mount over.
whatThisFixedComparedWithTheFirstAttempt.fix: The failed image had no mount-point directories for the kernel's virtual filesystems, so PID 1 could not mount /proc, /sys or /dev and froze before identifying itself. The successor image's builder creates them, along with the /run and /tmp the same startup needs.

whatWorked: The kernel started from the sealed image, with no initrd, on Virtualization.framework.
The ext4 filesystem mounted read-only from /dev/vda and the kernel reported the root mounted.
systemd 255.4-1ubuntu8 ran as PID 1, identified itself, and detected arm64 and a virtual machine.
The five mount-point directories the successor image added were enough: PID 1 mounted /proc, /sys and /dev and did not freeze, which is exactly where the first attempt stopped.
The guest reached sysinit.target, basic.target, multi-user.target and its default graphical.target.
Exactly one unit entered a failed state, ldconfig.service, for the read-only root the run requires.
The sealed root disk hashed identically before and after, so the read-only attachment held.
No host process, socket or temporary file of the machine outlived the run.
whatWouldBeNeededNext: an account database in the image, so systemd-sysusers has the boole-node and boole-native-checker identities to resolve on a read-only root
the runtime rootfs and content manifest under /var/lib/boole the launcher verifies before it serves anything
a readable path for the launcher's own output, so where it refuses stops being invisible
an authenticated host-guest transport, which is MAC.4 and is not started here
